[A|I]=[1−2100201]___________∼[1−21001012]___________∼[101101012]

b

decision.explanation: First divide row 2 by 2 to obtain [0,1,0,1/2]. Then add twice row 2 to row 1, obtaining [1,0,1,1]. These are the operations in option d.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $A$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We write down $A$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $A$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${A}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

content.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $A$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We write down $A$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $A$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${A}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $S$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${S}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[S\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We write down $S$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $S$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[S\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${S}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{S}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix Calculated Using Row Operations
content.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $S$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${S}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[S\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We write down $S$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $S$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[S\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${S}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{S}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

after.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${A}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We write down $A$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $A$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${A}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix Calculated Using Row Operations
content.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${A}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+6{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We write down $A$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $A$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+6{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${A}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 6\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $A$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We write down $A$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $A$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{1}↔{R}_{2},\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}.
$$

The matrix ${A}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

EXPLANATION

We write down A and the identity matrix I side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix A into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

[A|I]=[−21101001]R1↔R2∼[1001−2110]R2:=R2+2R1∼[10010112]

The matrix A−1 is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore,

content.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $A$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We write down $A$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $A$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{1}↔{R}_{2},\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}.
$$

The matrix ${A}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$
